hero.title: About EduChain
hero.subtitle: The platform in detail — architecture, smart contracts, security mechanisms and technology stack. Everything is publicly verifiable and running on the GembaBlockchain testnet.

overview.title: Overview
overview.p1: EduChain is a safe Web3 sandbox built on the GembaBlockchain testnet. The platform is composed of 7 interconnected smart contracts covering access control, digital assets, peer-to-peer trading, leaderboards and test GMB distribution.
overview.p2: All contracts are written in Solidity 0.8.28, compiled against the Cancun EVM, and use audited primitives from OpenZeppelin v5. Every contract is publicly verified on GembaScan and the source code can be reviewed line by line.
overview.p3: The frontend is a React 19 + TypeScript application with Tailwind v4, hosted on Hetzner with a Cloudflare CDN. Blockchain interaction is via wagmi + viem + ethers.

journey.title: How the platform is used
journey.subtitle: The student journey — from zero to leaderboard participant.

step1.title: Whitelist approval
step1.body: An administrator (teacher or coordinator) adds the student's address to the Whitelist contract. Without this approval, every other contract refuses interaction.

step2.title: Claim test GMB
step2.body: From the ETHFaucet the student claims 0.05 GMB every 24 hours. These funds are used for gas fees on subsequent transactions.

step3.title: Buy GAME tokens and mint NFTs
step3.body: In the Token Shop the student buys GAME tokens with test GMB or mints their own NFTs — predefined or with personal content uploaded to IPFS.

step4.title: Trade in the marketplace
step4.body: In the Marketplace the student lists tokens or NFTs for sale, buys from other students, or accepts private deals with a specific buyer.

step5.title: Climb the leaderboard
step5.body: TrackingContract reads balances in real time and computes points: 1 point per GAME token, 10 per predefined NFT, 30 per custom NFT. Tiers from Bronze to Platinum are based on the total.

contracts.title: Eight smart contracts
contracts.subtitle: Each contract has a clear responsibility and publicly verifiable source code.

whitelist.title: Whitelist
whitelist.body: A registry of approved addresses, a blacklist for suspended users and multiple administrators. All other contracts consult it before allowing an action. Uses OpenZeppelin EnumerableSet for O(1) membership checks.

gameToken.title: GameToken
gameToken.body: A fungible token that whitelisted users buy with test GMB at a fixed price. Three independent rate limits: max tokens per purchase, max purchases per day, max tokens per day. Per-user accounting is packed into a single storage slot for gas efficiency.

gameNFTPredefined.title: GameNFTPredefined
gameNFTPredefined.body: An NFT collection with predefined metadata. The URI follows a deterministic template of baseURI + tokenId + ".json". ERC-721A enables gas-efficient batch minting of multiple NFTs in a single transaction.

gameNFTCustom.title: GameNFTCustom
gameNFTCustom.body: Lets users provide their own IPFS URI when minting. Supports two payment modes: with test GMB or with GAME tokens. The URI is stored permanently after minting — guaranteed immutability of metadata.

marketplace.title: TokenMarketplace
marketplace.body: Supports listings of ERC-20 tokens and ERC-721 NFTs. Assets are escrowed in the marketplace during the listing and transferred to the buyer on purchase. Optional private listings restrict the sale to a specific address.

tracking.title: TrackingContract
tracking.body: A real-time aggregator: reads balances directly from the GameToken and NFT contracts on every request, computes points via an owner-configurable formula, and returns derived metrics (total points, tier, net worth in GMB). No cached state.

faucet.title: ETHFaucet
faucet.body: Dispenses a fixed amount of GMB to whitelisted users at intervals. Cooldown is enforced in seconds. Contract-level caps prevent configuration errors: the amount cannot exceed 1 GMB and the cooldown cannot exceed a week.

security.title: Security
security.subtitle: Multi-layer defence — at the smart-contract level, at the platform level, at the classroom level.

contractLayer.title: At the smart-contract level
contractLayer.item1: OpenZeppelin v5 primitives — Ownable, ReentrancyGuard, SafeERC20
contractLayer.item2: Custom errors instead of revert strings for gas efficiency
contractLayer.item3: Checks-Effects-Interactions pattern in every state-changing function
contractLayer.item4: Ownership renunciation (renounceOwnership) explicitly disabled — accidental loss of access is impossible
contractLayer.item5: Source code verified on GembaScan — open to audit by anyone

platformLayer.title: At the platform level
platformLayer.item1: We never request or receive private keys or seed phrases
platformLayer.item2: TLS-encrypted traffic across the entire site
platformLayer.item3: No user-profile database; the only personal data is the certificate data, minimal and time-limited
platformLayer.item4: Cloudflare DDoS protection and anti-bot on forms
platformLayer.item5: Exclusively testnet operations — real funds are never exchanged

classroomLayer.title: At the classroom level
classroomLayer.item1: Whitelist-based access — only approved students can interact
classroomLayer.item2: The teacher removes a student with one click — immediate access revocation
classroomLayer.item3: Rate limits in the contracts prevent fast or large mistakes
classroomLayer.item4: Admin panel for real-time activity monitoring

hero.title: A partnership for Web3 education in Europe
hero.subtitle: EduChain provides a ready-made, safe and pedagogically sound framework for introducing blockchain literacy into your institution. We are open to different forms of collaboration — from pilot projects and joint applications to European programmes, through to forking the platform for local needs.

intro.title: Why Web3 literacy is now unavoidable
intro.p1: Over the past thirty years the internet has moved from Web1 (static pages we read), through Web2 (platforms where we write and publish), to Web3 — an internet where digital ownership, identity and value are attested mathematically and on-chain.
intro.p2: The European Central Bank is preparing the digital euro. The European Union has an official regulatory framework for digital assets, a European Blockchain Services Infrastructure (EBSI), and a European digital-identity wallet programme. Web3 competencies will soon be basic digital literacy, not an exotic skill.
intro.p3: The question is not whether European students and young people will encounter Web3, but whether they will be prepared. The task of the education system — schools, universities, vocational-training colleges, community organisations and relevant ministries — is to prepare them safely, methodically and before they meet real risk.

benefits.title: What the partnership may bring your institution
benefits.subtitle: EduChain is designed to serve a broad range of educational institutions — primary and secondary schools, universities, vocational-training colleges, community organisations and relevant ministries. The model of collaboration is configured to the specific context and needs of each partner.

director.title: For the leadership
director.body: A potential coordinator or partner role in international educational projects — depending on the project design. Positioning of the institution among the leaders in innovative digital education. A new European project in the institutional portfolio.

school.title: For the institution
school.body: Institutional income when acting as coordinator or partner in a project. Potential modernisation of the material base — equipment, software, a dedicated space. International mobilities subject to project funding. Status as an early adopter of Web3 education in the region.

teachers.title: For the teachers
teachers.body: Remuneration for official functions in the project. Free professional training and a pathway to an official certificate in Web3 and blockchain literacy. International mobilities subject to project funding. Development in a field that will be in strong demand over the coming decade.

students.title: For students and learners
students.body: Free hands-on exposure to the technologies that will dominate the digital economy. An individual Web3 literacy certificate — a 20-question exam, a PDF by e-mail and a non-transferable record on the blockchain. International mobilities subject to project funding. A real advantage when applying for jobs or higher education in the IT sector.

howItWorks.title: How the partnership may unfold
howItWorks.subtitle: An illustrative path in three stages — from an informal introduction to a full European project. The specific model and timeline are agreed to your context.

step1.title: Informal pilot
step1.body: Training a small team of teachers or mentors at your institution and running an after-school course, elective or workshops with a limited number of learners. Collecting practical experience and documentation for the next stage. Cost to the institution — minimal or zero; the main resources are provided by GEMBA IT.

step2.title: Joint application
step2.body: Preparation and submission of a project proposal to a suitable European or national programme (Erasmus+ KA220, Digital Europe, Horizon Europe, national recovery instruments and others). The roles of coordinator and partner are allocated according to the specific project design. Additional partners may be included — other institutions, NGOs or international organisations.

step3.title: Execution
step3.body: A multi-year project with clearly allocated roles, budgets and responsibilities — platform development, teacher training, mobilities where applicable, dissemination of results, building an open educational resource base.

programmes.title: Alignment with European programmes
programmes.subtitle: EduChain is designed to meet the criteria of the main European and national funds for digital education. The applicable programme depends on the specific type of institution and project design.

erasmus.title: Erasmus+ KA220
erasmus.body: The teacher-training curriculum and cross-institutional partnerships fit the criteria for cooperation in school, vocational and higher education.

digital.title: Digital Europe Programme
digital.body: EduChain aligns with the “Digital Skills” priority, especially advanced digital skills in emerging technologies.

horizon.title: Horizon Europe
horizon.body: The research potential (gamification, on-chain credentials, pedagogy for decentralised systems) matches Cluster 2 and Cluster 4.

national.title: National recovery plans
national.body: Most member states have earmarked funds for digital education. EduChain is a ready-made solution that can be integrated directly into those plans.

safety.title: Safety and compliance
safety.subtitle: EduChain is an educational tool — not a financial product.

testnet.title: Testnet only
testnet.body: The platform runs entirely on the GembaBlockchain testnet. Real money is never exchanged. Learners experiment with zero financial risk.

gdpr.title: GDPR compliance
gdpr.body: Only the minimum necessary data is collected. The principles of transparency, purpose limitation and privacy by design apply throughout.

financial.title: Not a financial instrument
financial.body: GameToken has no real market value and is not traded on external markets. The platform is classified as an educational tool.

supervision.title: Full pedagogical supervision
supervision.body: Teachers have an admin panel for whitelist control, the points leaderboard and instant access revocation if needed. Transaction rate limits prevent abuse.

q1.q: What financial commitments are required from the institution?
q1.a: For the informal pilot — minimal or zero; most resources are provided by GEMBA IT. For joint applications to European programmes, the financial model depends on the specific instrument; most Erasmus+ lines, for example, do not require co-financing from the institution, and funds are managed by the coordinating party. Specific conditions are agreed per project.

q2.q: How much time per week will it take the teachers?
q2.a: During the informal pilot: 2–3 hours per week (one after-school session plus preparation). When running a full project, the volume depends on the role, but on average 4–8 hours per week — with potential for additional remuneration subject to project funding.

q3.q: Do the teachers need special prior knowledge before starting?
q3.a: No. EduChain envisages a 3-day intensive training programme (or its equivalent online course) with a pathway to a Web3 educator certificate. No prior blockchain knowledge is required.

q4.q: What happens if the joint project is not approved?
q4.a: The informal pilot continues regardless of the outcome. The application can be improved and submitted again under the same or another suitable programme. The experience gained during the pilot phase remains valuable to the institution and its teachers.

q5.q: Who is legally responsible for the students when they use the platform?
q5.a: The institution retains its standard pedagogical responsibility. EduChain runs in a controlled environment (testnet, no real money, whitelist-based access) designed to be safer than ordinary internet access in an informatics lesson.

q6.q: Can EduChain be integrated into the existing curriculum?
q6.a: Yes. The 16-hour student programme is modular and can fit as an elective, an after-school club, a university module, or a component of existing subjects such as informatics, economics or e-commerce.

cta.title: Ready for a conversation?
cta.subtitle: I offer an on-site meeting at your institution or an online demonstration — about 60 minutes. No commitment, no closed documents. Just a conversation between people who want to change education.

hero.title: EduChain in the classroom
hero.subtitle: A teaching framework, training and a pathway to certification that prepare you to teach Web3 and blockchain. No prior knowledge of the subject required — the programme is designed to train teachers first and students second.

philosophy.title: Teachers train first
philosophy.body: Students cannot be led through Web3 by someone who has not personally mastered the technology. This is a core principle of EduChain. That is why — before any work with students — teachers are expected to complete a full course, with a pathway to a certificate and the time to feel confident in the environment.

whoFor.title: Who the programme is for
whoFor.subtitle: Web3 is not a new subject — it is a natural extension of disciplines already taught in schools, universities and vocational training centres.

it.title: Educators of informatics and programming
it.body: You see smart contracts in working Solidity code, transactions on GembaScan and security practices. EduChain is an application of OOP and Web3 concepts you already teach.

ecommerce.title: Educators of e-commerce
ecommerce.body: EduChain's decentralised marketplace is a real example of peer-to-peer trading without an intermediary. Students see alternatives to the Amazon and eBay models.

economics.title: Educators of economics and entrepreneurship
economics.body: Tokens and NFTs are living lessons in ownership, scarcity, pricing and gamification. The internal economy of the platform is a microeconomic experiment.

design.title: Educators of graphic design and media
design.body: NFTs are digital creative works with metadata. Students create an image, write a JSON description, publish it on IPFS — a digital portfolio with provable ownership.

training.title: Training for teachers
training.subtitle: Two planned formats, equivalent in terms of certification — choose the one that suits you when the respective session is launched.

inPerson.title: In-person intensive — 3 days
inPerson.body: A planned in-person programme in a regional centre, included in the pilot phases of the project. Participants are expected to arrive with a laptop and finish with a pathway to a certificate, a configured wallet and hands-on experience with the live platform.
inPerson.day1Body: The evolution of the internet (Web1→Web2→Web3). How blockchain works — consensus, immutability, why decentralisation matters. MetaMask installation, configuration, protecting private keys. The first real transaction on GembaBlockchain. Gas fees and transaction mechanics via GembaScan.
inPerson.day2Title: Day 2 — Smart contracts and digital assets
inPerson.day2Body: The ERC-20 standard (fungible tokens) and the ERC-721 standard (unique objects). Each participant mints their first NFT. IPFS as decentralised storage — uploading through EduChain's own node straight from the platform, obtaining a content identifier, linking it to a smart contract. The marketplace — listing, buying, cancelling.
inPerson.day3Body: The EduChain admin panel — student whitelisting, progress monitoring, responding to classroom incidents. Security — spotting scams, what an approve function really authorises. Integrating AI assistants as analytical tools. A practical assessment.

online.title: Self-paced online course
online.body: Eight modules, about 15 hours of video in total, interactive exercises and a graded practical assignment. Topics mirror the in-person course. Each module ends with a test (70% to pass), the final test requires 80%. Regular Q&A webinars with the EduChain team and a community forum for peer-to-peer support are planned. On successful completion, the pathway to a certificate is equivalent to the in-person course.

certification.title: What we plan for you to receive
certification.subtitle: A pathway to certification with real value and ongoing support when the project is realised.

cert.title: Web3 educator certificate
cert.body: Planned issuance by GEMBA IT in the form of a signed PDF and an on-chain NFT credential. Annual re-certification is planned to reflect the evolution of Web3 standards.

community.title: A peer network
community.body: A planned community of certified teachers — a forum, periodic meetups, sharing of good practice and classroom materials. The network will grow alongside the adoption of the platform.

support.title: Priority support
support.body: When working within an active project or formal partnership — a priority channel of contact with the EduChain team, so that you are not left alone in front of your students when something does not work as expected.

development.title: Professional development
development.body: Planned periodic updates on Web3 news. Recognition for participation in international mobilities and conferences under the relevant project programmes (Erasmus+, Digital Europe and others).

curriculum.title: What you teach your students
curriculum.subtitle: A 16-hour programme in 7 modules — from concept to independent project.

m1.title: Introduction to Web3 and blockchain fundamentals
m1.body: Evolution of the internet. Blockchain as a shared public ledger. Decentralisation, transparency, immutability. Smart contracts through the vending-machine analogy. First MetaMask connection to GembaBlockchain.

m2.title: Web3 wallets and smart contracts in practice
m2.body: Private keys, seed phrases, what never to do with them. How transactions are signed. Watching a transaction in the mempool and on GembaScan. First claim of test GMB and first GAME token purchase.

m3.title: ERC-20 tokens and decentralised trading
m3.body: What makes a token fungible. Total supply vs. circulating supply. Liquidity pools and price discovery. Buying and selling GAME tokens on the platform.

m4.title: NFTs and digital art (ERC-721)
m4.body: What makes a token unique. Metadata and IPFS. Every student creates an original image, writes a JSON description, uploads it through the platform to EduChain's own IPFS node and mints their first NFT.

m5.title: Token and NFT economics
m5.body: Asset transfer, approval, listing on the marketplace. Pricing digital assets. A timed leaderboard race — who will reach the highest tier.

m6.title: Security, key management and scam detection
m6.body: Phishing, fake airdrops, malicious approve functions, rug pulls. Reading contract source on GembaScan. A simulated scam in the classroom — the student must recognise the attack before signing. Those who do not succeed learn more than those who do.

m7.title: Final project and AI as a blockchain assistant
m7.body: Using AI assistants for contract analysis — not to replace the student's judgement but to strengthen it. An individual project: an NFT collection with a narrative, a leaderboard strategy, a marketplace plan. Presentation to the class.

outcome.title: Learning outcomes
outcome.body: A student who completes the programme can: explain the fundamentals of blockchain; create and protect a Web3 wallet; read and interpret on-chain transactions; create and publish original digital assets; recognise scams; use AI tools for contract analysis; describe the economic dynamics of tokenised systems; and present a complete Web3 project to an audience.

tools.title: The tools you get
tools.subtitle: The teacher is not alone in the classroom.

admin.title: Admin panel
admin.body: One-click student whitelisting. Real-time monitoring of every student. Remove from whitelist when needed — instant access revocation.

limits.title: Built-in limits
limits.body: Transaction limits (3 purchases per day, 3 mints per day, 1 claim per 24 hours). Students cannot make a large mistake or spam the system.

monitoring.title: Live leaderboard
monitoring.body: You see every student's progress in a live on-chain leaderboard. You can easily spot who needs extra help and who is ready for harder tasks.

materials.title: Ready-made materials
materials.body: Lesson plans, classroom exercises, tests, example scenarios, common problems and solutions. You get everything you need to run the lesson.

q1.q: I have never worked with blockchain. Can I manage?
q1.a: Yes. The programme is designed specifically for teachers with no prior knowledge. The planned 3-day course (or its online equivalent) starts from zero — from installing MetaMask to administering a live platform. No prior blockchain knowledge is required.

q2.q: How much weekly time will teaching take?
q2.a: The lesson itself is 1–2 hours per week. Preparation for the first lessons is more demanding (2–3 hours for the first 3–4 modules) but then drops to 30–60 minutes. Ready-made lesson plans are planned — you are not writing a curriculum from scratch.

q3.q: What do I do if a student asks a technical question I do not know?
q3.a: First — that is normal. Even experts do not know everything about blockchain. Second — within an active partnership or project, a priority support channel with the EduChain team is planned. Third — the integrated AI assistant in the curriculum is exactly for this: students learn to use AI as a research tool, not for you to know everything.

q4.q: Is it safe for my children to work with blockchain?
q4.a: The platform runs entirely on the GembaBlockchain testnet — real money is never exchanged. Tokens and NFTs have no real value. Whitelist-based access means only your students use the platform. Transaction limits prevent abuse. This is a more controlled environment than ordinary internet access in an informatics lesson.

q5.a: When a full project with secured funding is realised — yes, under contract. The volume depends on the role (lead teacher, co-teacher, mobility mentor and so on) and on the specific programme (Erasmus+, Digital Europe, national instruments). Rates are agreed individually with the institution and the coordinating party and typically fall within the realistic range for European educational projects.

q6.q: Can I use EduChain outside a formal project?
q6.a: Yes. The platform and learning materials are open (open source, Creative Commons) — any trained teacher may use them in class without waiting for a formal project. Project funding brings additional remuneration, mobilities and wider scope, but is not required for teaching.

hero.title: Philosophy and principles
hero.subtitle: Why EduChain is built the way it is — for teachers, for students, for the Web3 community and for the long-term sustainability of the digital economy.

infrastructure.title: Education is core infrastructure
infrastructure.body1: The digital economy is only as strong as the people who use, build and understand it. Every long-term goal — safe asset stewardship, resilient public goods, critical thinking in decentralised systems — depends on a steady pipeline of educated users.
infrastructure.body2: EduChain closes a structural gap. Most European school curricula still treat Web3 as a niche topic, if they treat it at all. EduChain delivers a complete, classroom-ready programme: production-grade smart contracts on GembaBlockchain, a 16-hour student curriculum, a teacher-training pathway and a polished, multilingual web application.
infrastructure.body3: Non-commercial, vendor-neutral, open to fork. EduChain does not extract value — it turns every cohort of trained teachers into a multiplier that reaches hundreds of students over time.

publicGood.title: Public-good principles
publicGood.subtitle: Every design decision in EduChain reflects the values of genuine open-source principle.

mit.title: MIT licence for the code
mit.body: The smart contracts are MIT-licensed — free to copy, modify and use commercially. Any school, university or community can fork EduChain for its own country, language or context.

cc.title: Creative Commons for learning materials
cc.body: The 16-hour curriculum, teacher training and all pedagogical resources are under Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0. Adaptations preserve the same licence — knowledge stays open.

noToken.title: No token, no fees
noToken.body: EduChain has no token for sale, no paid tiers, no premium features. The GAME tokens inside the platform have no monetary value — they are a pedagogical instrument.

nonExtractive.title: Non-extractive design
nonExtractive.body: GEMBA EOOD operates as project steward, not rent-seeker. All funding goes directly into development, training and ecosystem growth — never to dividends or expansion outside the mission.

canonical.title: Canonical Web3 standards
canonical.subtitle: EduChain uses only established, portable technologies. Nothing patented, nothing proprietary.

standards.title: Ethereum standards
standards.body: ERC-20 for fungible tokens, ERC-721 and ERC-721A for NFTs, EIP-1559 gas mechanics, OpenZeppelin v5 security primitives. Students learn standards that work everywhere — not the features of a specific commercial product.

portable.title: Portable skills
portable.body: What students learn in EduChain applies directly to mainnet Ethereum, any EVM-compatible Layer 2 (Arbitrum, Optimism, Base, zkSync) or an enterprise consortium chain. Nothing is locked to a specific platform.

verified.title: Verified on GembaScan
verified.body: All eight smart contracts are verified on GembaScan. Students, teachers, auditors and evaluators can read the exact code that runs on-chain — no trusted frontend required. Full public transparency.

modernStack.title: Modern frontend stack
modernStack.body: React 19, TypeScript, wagmi, viem, i18next. Multilingual (BG/EN/ES), keyboard-accessible, mobile-optimised. Designed to be the first Web3 application a 12-year-old student ever uses.

testnetFirst.title: Testnet realism
testnetFirst.body1: EduChain runs entirely on the GembaBlockchain testnet. No exceptions, no mainnet bridges, no mixing with real funds. This is a deliberate choice — students interact with exactly the technology that powers real blockchain networks, but without financial exposure.
testnetFirst.body2: Every transaction is a real GembaBlockchain transaction. Real gas, real mempool, real GembaScan visibility. The only difference: the value is notional — test GMB has no monetary value outside the experimental environment.
testnetFirst.body3: This makes EduChain safer than ordinary internet access in a computing class. Whitelist-based access, transaction rate limits and the ability for a teacher to remove a student instantly — every layer is designed for a controlled educational setting.

roadmap.title: Phased, realistic growth
roadmap.subtitle: EduChain does not promise a revolution. It promises sustained, measurable, step-by-step growth.

phase0.label: Phase 0 — Ready infrastructure
phase0.body: The platform is deployed and working. 8 verified smart contracts on GembaBlockchain. A 16-hour curriculum translated into Bulgarian. A web application in three languages. A GitHub repository open under the MIT licence. Initial conversations with a Bulgarian school.

phase1.label: Phase 1 — Pilot year
phase1.body: Pilot deployment in 1 Bulgarian school. 10 trained and certified teachers. 250 students completing the 16-hour programme. Documentation, feedback loops and a case study for the next phases.

phase2.label: Phase 2 — European expansion
phase2.body: Expansion to 3–5 schools across 3 EU member states. 30 certified teachers. 750 students completed. Translation into 5 European languages. Partnership with an external evaluation organisation. Potential Erasmus+ KA220 funding.

phase3.label: Phase 3 — Scaling and recognition
phase3.body: 15–20 partner schools. 100+ certified teachers. 2,500+ students reached. First academic publications. Conversations about national recognition of the certificate. Translations into 10+ languages. A sustainable community of forked variants.

sustainability.title: Sustainability beyond any single funder
sustainability.body1: EduChain is designed so that no single source of funding or organisation is a single point of failure. If GEMBA EOOD steps back, the project continues — the open code and learning materials allow any organisation to take on stewardship.
sustainability.body2: Funding is non-dilutive — grants from European programmes, public-goods funding, institutional partnerships. No token sale, no equity investors, no pressure for a commercial pivot.
sustainability.body3: The long-term vision is a network of institutions — schools, universities, ministries, community organisations — mutually supporting Web3 education in Europe. EduChain is just one instrument, not the centre of that network.

cta.title: Open to conversation
cta.subtitle: EduChain is ready to be evaluated, piloted, forked or integrated into a broader educational initiative. Whether you are a school, a funder, a researcher or a developer — we look forward to connecting.

hero.title: Privacy Policy
hero.subtitle: EduChain is designed not to require and not to collect personal data. There is one deliberate exception: a certificate carries a name, so certificate data is collected and kept for a stated period. This document describes exactly what happens to information — briefly, without templates and without evasions.

summary.title: Short summary
summary.body: There is no registration with a name or e-mail and there is no user database. We do not store contact messages on the server. We use no analytics, no advertising trackers and no profiling. You connect with a Web3 wallet, which is pseudonymous by default. The ONE exception: if you ask for an exam certificate we keep your three names, position, organisation and e-mail — the e-mail only until the certificate has been sent, the rest for as long as the certificate has to remain verifiable (5 years). No personal data whatsoever goes onto the blockchain — only a hash.

section1.title: 1. Data controller
section1.body: In the cases in which we process personal data within the meaning of the GDPR (Regulation (EU) 2016/679), the controller is GEMBA EOOD (referred to here as “GEMBA IT”), a Bulgarian company with UIC 208656371, headquartered in Varna, Bulgaria. Contact for privacy questions: contacts@gembait.com.

section2.title: 2. What we do NOT collect
section2.intro: What EduChain deliberately does not do:
section2.item1: We do not require registration with a name, email, password or other personal information
section2.item2: We have no user database — no “users” table, no passwords and no profiles. The only database that exists is the one for certificates (see section 3), and you only enter it by asking for a certificate yourself
section2.item3: We do not store contact-form e-mails on our server — they are forwarded straight to our mailbox and do not stay in the platform's infrastructure
section2.item4: We do not use Google Analytics, Facebook Pixel, or any other analytics or tracking system
section2.item5: We do not profile users or display advertising
section2.item6: We do not sell, rent or share personal data with third parties for marketing purposes

section3.title: 3. What actually happens
section3.intro: Here is exactly what information passes through the platform and what happens with it:
section3.walletBody: When you connect MetaMask or another wallet, your browser reveals the public address (e.g. 0x1234…abcd) to the platform. This address is public information on the blockchain and does not identify you as an individual. Your private keys and seed phrase never leave your browser and are never sent to us.
section3.contactBody: If you write to us through the site form, what you fill in (name, email, message) is forwarded directly to our email via SMTP. Messages are not written to any database on the server. After receipt they remain in our inbox — for replying and handling your enquiry.
section3.browserBody: Your browser stores locally (in localStorage) your language preference, theme (light/dark) and the wagmi session for the active wallet. This information is not sent to us — it lives only in your browser and is deleted when you clear site data.
section3.blockchainBody: Every transaction you make (test-GMB claim, token purchase, NFT minting, trading) is recorded publicly on the GembaBlockchain testnet blockchain. This is inherent to the technology — not an EduChain choice. Blockchain records are public and irreversible by design.
section3.certificatesTitle: Exam certificates (the only place with personal data)
section3.certificatesBody: If you decide to sit the certificate exam, you enter three names, an e-mail, a position and an organisation. The names, the position and the organisation are printed on the certificate and shown on the public verification page — that is the point of a certificate: a third party has to be able to check it. The e-mail does two things: it confirms your address with a code, and it delivers the certificate as a PDF. After it has been sent, the e-mail is deleted and only a salted hash (HMAC) of it remains — enough to enforce the limit of 3 attempts a day, useless for reaching you. An attempt that produced no certificate is deleted in full after 30 days. An issued certificate is kept for 5 years, after which only the serial, the date and the score remain and the names are dropped. 🔑 NO personal data goes onto the blockchain: only a hash (keccak256) of the certificate's contents, the serial, the date and the score. The hash makes it possible to prove that a certificate you are shown is exactly the one that was issued, and makes it impossible to recover anything from it.

section4.title: 4. Server and CDN logs
section4.intro: Like every website, EduChain passes through infrastructure layers that keep technical logs:
section4.cloudflareBody: Cloudflare processes every request before it reaches our server and keeps its own logs (IP address, User-Agent, page requested). Those logs are managed by Cloudflare under their privacy policy and are not under our control. We use Cloudflare for acceleration and protection — an alternative would make the site slow and vulnerable.
section4.apacheBody: Our web server (Apache on Hetzner) may keep standard access logs with IP addresses and requested paths for a limited period, as needed for troubleshooting and security. These logs are not linked to user profiles (because there are none) and are not used for any analytics or commercial purpose.
section4.turnstileBody: The contact form runs Cloudflare Turnstile — an anti-bot check that verifies whether the request comes from a real human. Turnstile may inspect your browser and temporarily set a technical cookie. The check is performed by Cloudflare and we receive no details about you.

section5.title: 5. Legal basis for processing
section5.intro: When we do process data (contact-form emails, technical logs), the GDPR legal bases are:
section5.item1: Consent (Art. 6(1)(a)) — when filling the contact form you explicitly provide your data so we can reply
section5.item2: Legitimate interest (Art. 6(1)(f)) — maintaining technical logs for security and troubleshooting
section5.item3: Legal obligation (Art. 6(1)(c)) — complying with any court order or statutory duty
section5.item4: Contract and legitimate interest (Art. 6(1)(b) and (f)) — for certificates: without a name there is no certificate, and a third party's ability to verify it is the whole purpose

section6.title: 6. Your rights under GDPR
section6.intro: To the extent we process any information about you, you have the following rights:
section6.right1: Right of access — to know whether we store information about you and what it is
section6.right2: Right to rectification — to request correction of inaccurate data
section6.right3: Right to erasure — to request deletion of contact-form messages still in our inbox
section6.right6: Right to lodge a complaint with the Bulgarian Commission for Personal Data Protection (CPDP, cpdp.bg)
section6.contact: To exercise these rights — write to contacts@gembait.com. We reply within 30 days.
section6.blockchainNote: Important: blockchain transactions cannot technically be deleted. This is the nature of the technology — not a GEMBA IT decision.
section6.right7: The right to have certificate data erased — write to us and we will remove the name, position and organisation from our record; the serial, the date and the score remain, so that an already issued and verified certificate is not made meaningless, and the hash on the blockchain is technically impossible to delete (see the note below)

section7.title: 7. Minors
section7.body: EduChain can be used by students aged 12 and above in the context of organised school learning under teacher supervision. Because we require no personal data (and no name-based registration), the platform collects no child-specific information — unlike most internet services where a student would have to create a profile with personal details. Parents and teachers can contact us at contacts@gembait.com with any questions about child safety on the platform.

section8.title: 8. Security
section8.body: All traffic to the platform goes over TLS (HTTPS), with HSTS and a strict Content-Security-Policy. The certificate database is the only place with personal data: it is a file on the server readable only by the application process, it holds the minimum, and it is cleared on a schedule. The key with which the server records certificates on the blockchain can only ISSUE — it cannot revoke and it cannot change roles; revocation is signed with a separate, cold key that is not on the server. In the event of a security incident we will notify the competent supervisory authorities and the affected individuals under Articles 33 and 34 GDPR within 72 hours.

section9.title: 9. Changes to this policy
section9.body: We may update this policy if the platform, the law or our infrastructure changes. The last-updated date is at the top of the document. For material changes we will place a notice on the home page.

hero.title: What students learn in EduChain
hero.subtitle: A structured curriculum for students aged 12 and above. From the first blockchain connection to an individual final project presented to the class. Free, open and adaptable to any learning context.

philosophy.title: Learning by doing
philosophy.p1: EduChain does not explain blockchain at the whiteboard — it lets students experience it themselves. Every concept is tried in a safe test environment, with real blockchain transactions and zero financial risk.
philosophy.p2: Theory comes after practice. The student first sees what happens, then understands why — and that is the order in which knowledge sticks. Every module follows this principle: practice, then reflection.

overview.title: The programme in numbers
overview.subtitle: A 16-hour curriculum structured for one school term or a short intensive.

modules.title: Seven modules — from introduction to an independent project
modules.subtitle: Every module builds on the previous one. The progression leads from basic concepts to independent creation.

m1.title: Introduction to Web3
m1.description: The student takes a tour through the history of the internet — from static Web1 pages, through Web2 platforms, to decentralised Web3 networks. Core concepts are introduced: shared public ledger, immutability, decentralisation. The smart contract is presented through the vending-machine analogy — simple, accessible, memorable.
m1.outcome: The student can explain the difference between Web1, Web2 and Web3 to a classmate.

m2.title: First contact with blockchain
m2.description: Installing and configuring MetaMask. Understanding what private keys and seed phrases really are — and what must never be done with them. The student claims their first test GMB from the platform faucet and performs their first blockchain transaction. They follow it on GembaScan — watching with their own eyes as it is confirmed on the network.
m2.outcome: The student has a working Web3 wallet and understands how to protect it.

m3.title: Tokens and decentralised economy
m3.description: What makes a token — what fungible means, exactly how many tokens exist, how price is determined. The student buys GAME tokens on the platform, watches their balance change in real time and understands what sits behind each number — not just a figure in a database, but a publicly recorded entry on the blockchain.
m3.outcome: The student understands how digital currencies work as an economic system.

m4.title: Digital ownership and NFTs
m4.description: The difference between unique and fungible — why an NFT is not “a picture on the blockchain” but something deeper. The student creates an original image, writes a description with attributes in JSON, uploads it to IPFS (a decentralised file system) and mints their first NFT. For the first time they have a digital work that is provably theirs — not in a platform account, but on the blockchain.
m4.outcome: The student owns their first NFT, created from scratch — theirs, forever.

m5.title: Market, competition, strategy
m5.description: The student lists an NFT for sale on the marketplace. They buy from classmates. They understand how to value a digital work — what is unique worth? A timed race at the end of the lesson: who will reach the highest tier? Gamification turns economic concepts into a strategic game.
m5.outcome: The student understands the market logic of digital assets — supply, demand, value.

m6.title: Security and scam detection
m6.description: This is the module parents will thank you for. A detailed look at common scams: phishing, fake airdrops, malicious approve functions, rug pulls. The student learns to read smart-contract source code on GembaScan and to spot suspicious signals. At the end of the lesson — a simulated attack in the classroom: students must recognise the vector before signing a transaction. Those who do not succeed learn more than those who do.
m6.outcome: The student can defend themselves in the real Web3 world — not out of fear, but from knowledge.

m7.title: Final project
m7.description: Two hours working with AI assistants as analytical tools — the student learns to use them for code and decision analysis, not to replace their own judgement. Then two hours of independent work on an individual project: an NFT collection with a narrative, a leaderboard strategy, a marketplace plan. The course ends with a presentation to the class. Issuing an on-chain certificate at the end — an NFT credential that stays on the blockchain — is planned.
m7.outcome: The student has a completed Web3 project they can show (a certificate is planned).

formats.title: How the programme is delivered
formats.subtitle: 16 hours are modular — they adapt to different learning contexts.

weekly.title: Weekly elective
weekly.body: One lesson per week × 16 weeks = a full school term. The recommended option — enough time between lessons for reflection and independent work.

intensive.title: Intensive
intensive.body: 2–3 hours per week × 5–6 weeks. Suitable for holiday camps, STEM weeks or schools that want a fast introduction.

integrated.title: Integrated into a subject
integrated.body: Modules can be distributed across an existing subject — informatics, economics, e-commerce, entrepreneurship. Web3 as an extension, not a stand-alone subject.

extracurricular.title: Extracurricular club
extracurricular.body: No grades, no tests — a free format for students who want to learn of their own accord. Good for schools that are not yet ready to put it on the curriculum.

certificate.title: Web3 literacy certificate
certificate.subtitle: Planned: not just a document — an on-chain credential that stays publicly verifiable.

what.title: What the student receives
what.body: A planned dual certificate: a signed PDF document from GEMBA IT and an NFT credential recorded on the blockchain. The NFT will be immutable and can be shown in future CVs, university applications or Web3 portfolios.

why.title: Why this matters
why.body: At a time when every school issues paper certificates that can be forged or lost, the EduChain certificate will be publicly verifiable by anyone once it is issued. An employer or a university will be able to confirm authenticity with one click on GembaScan.

criteria.title: How it is earned
criteria.body: Completion of all 7 modules, active participation in practical exercises and presentation of the final project to the class. This is not a competition — since 31 October 2026, when the certificate module went live, every student who completes the programme will receive a certificate.

cta.title: How you can bring EduChain on board
cta.subtitle: The programme is free and open. You do not need a financial commitment to begin.
cta.schoolsBody: Get in touch for an Erasmus+ KA220 partnership — funding, international mobilities, certified teachers.
cta.teachersBody: Train as a Web3 educator through a 3-day intensive or an online course — certification is planned.
cta.exploreBody: Explore the environment students will work in — live leaderboard, marketplace, NFT gallery.

hero.title: EduChain in one minute
hero.subtitle: Shorter than the opening shot of a film. Behind every action on the platform stands a real blockchain transaction — safe, verifiable, forever.

videoPlaceholder.title: Video demonstration coming soon
videoPlaceholder.body: A 60-second summary of the platform — how a student connects, claims test GMB, mints their first NFT and climbs the leaderboard. It will be published in the coming days.

steps.title: How the platform works
steps.subtitle: Five steps — from the first connection to a visible result on the blockchain.

step1.title: Connecting a wallet
step1.body: The student connects MetaMask to EduChain. The platform sees only the public address — no registration, no password, no personal information.

step2.title: Claiming test GMB
step2.body: From the platform faucet the student receives 0.05 test GMB. This is the “fuel” for every following action — but it has no real monetary value.

step3.title: Buying GAME tokens
step3.body: With the test GMB the student buys GAME — the platform’s internal currency. Every transaction is recorded publicly on the blockchain and is verifiable on GembaScan.

step4.title: Creating an NFT
step4.body: The student mints a digital creative work — predefined or custom, with an image and IPFS metadata. The created NFT is their property forever.

step5.title: Climbing the leaderboard
step5.body: Every action earns points. The live leaderboard updates automatically. Gamification turns learning into healthy competition among classmates.

screenshots.title: Screenshots from the platform
screenshots.subtitle: Ten frames from the real experience — how EduChain looks for a student and a teacher.

home.title: Home page
home.body: The entrance to the platform — a quick overview of features and live blockchain statistics.

faucet.title: Test GMB faucet
faucet.body: The student claims 0.05 GMB every 24 hours. Cooldown, history and total balance are visible.

shop.title: Token and NFT shop
shop.body: Three kinds of purchase — GAME tokens, predefined NFTs or custom works via IPFS.

gallery.title: Student gallery
gallery.body: All owned digital assets in one place — with metadata, attributes and a direct link to the blockchain.

marketplace.title: Decentralised marketplace
marketplace.body: Peer-to-peer trading between students. Filter by asset type, private listings to specific buyers.

leaderboard.title: Live leaderboard
leaderboard.body: Top 10 players with tier badges. Refreshes automatically after every new transaction.

rankings.title: Full rankings
rankings.body: All participants with filters, sorting and search. Suitable for a class with many students.

connect.title: Connecting MetaMask
connect.body: Web3 login — no password, no email, no registration. The wallet is the identity.

transaction.title: Signing a transaction
transaction.body: The student always sees what they sign. Gas fees and details — transparent before confirmation.

etherscan.title: Proof on the blockchain
etherscan.body: Every transaction is publicly visible on GembaScan — verifiable by anyone, forever.

proof.title: Not a simulation — real blockchain technology
proof.body: EduChain uses the same technology that powers real blockchain networks. The only difference is that it uses a test network (GembaBlockchain) where tokens have no monetary value. Every transaction, every NFT, every purchase is a real record on the blockchain — transparent, immutable and publicly verifiable.

cta.title: Ready to try?
cta.subtitle: Contact us — we will add your wallet to the whitelist and give you access to the demonstration environment within half an hour.

certificates.title: Certificates
certificates.subtitle: A 20-question exam. 80 % or above earns a certificate.
certificates.intro: The exam covers the foundations: blockchain, wallets and keys, transactions and fees, smart contracts, security. Questions are drawn at random from a bank of {{bank}}, across three levels of difficulty.
certificates.how1: You fill in your details and confirm your e-mail with a code — a certificate only ever goes to a confirmed address.
certificates.how2: You answer {{n}} questions, one per screen. There is no going back and no changing an answer.
certificates.how3: At {{pass}} % or above the certificate arrives as a PDF by e-mail and is recorded on GembaBlockchain.
certificates.how4: The on-chain record is only a hash of the contents and a serial number — no personal data goes onto the chain.
certificates.privacyNote: We store the minimum: your three names, position, organisation and e-mail. The e-mail is kept only as long as it is needed — until the certificate is sent — and then only a salted hash remains, for the attempt limit. An attempt that produced no certificate is deleted after 30 days. Details: Privacy Policy.
certificates.formNote: These details will be printed on the certificate. Write them exactly as you want them to appear.
certificates.walletNote: The certificate will be issued to the connected wallet: {{wallet}}
certificates.codeSent: We have sent a six-digit code to {{email}}. It is valid for 15 minutes.
certificates.noBackWarning: Once you pick an answer there is no going back and no changing it.
certificates.expired: Time ran out for this sitting. You can start a new one.
certificates.noAnswersShown: We do not show which questions were wrong or what the right answers were — the same bank is used for your next attempt.
certificates.retry: You can try again after 24 hours (up to {{max}} attempts a day).
certificates.certMailed: The certificate has been e-mailed to you as a PDF.
certificates.certMailFailed: The certificate was issued but the e-mail did not go out. Download it from the link below, or write to us.
certificates.errInvalidName: Enter three names (letters, hyphens and apostrophes only).
certificates.errTurnstile: The anti-bot check did not pass. Please try again.
certificates.errAttemptLimit: You have reached the limit of {{max}} attempts for today. Try again tomorrow.
certificates.errTooManyCodes: Too many codes have been requested for this address. Try again tomorrow.
certificates.errCodeExpired: The code has expired. Start again.
certificates.errMail: The e-mail with the code could not be sent. Try again in a moment.
certificates.errChain: The on-chain record did not go through. Your result is saved — press “Finish the exam” again in a moment.
certificates.needWallet: Connect a wallet to start the exam — the certificate is issued to your address.

verify.title: Verify a certificate
verify.subtitle: Enter the serial from the certificate. The status is read straight from the chain.
verify.notFoundHint: Check the serial. It has the form EDU-YEAR-NUMBER.
verify.unreachable: The chain is not answering right now, so we cannot confirm validity. The details below come from our own record.
verify.minimised: The names have been removed under the retention period; the serial, the date and the score remain verifiable.
verify.noEmailNote: This page never shows an e-mail address.
